description:
Owner decision needed: should the oracle keep reading `author-family:<family>` labels at all? Options: (1) delete the `author_label_prefix` lookup and then either hard-code the claude exclusion or move sonnet last in the low-medium and medium-high orders; (2) keep the lookup and have PR tooling (`make pr-open` or the agent PR flow) apply the label; (3) keep today's behaviour (claude default) and document that diversity covers only claude authors. Recommendation: option 1. The label is a reviewer-steering lever that any agent holding the token can set, so it does not tell the oracle who wrote the change. Inferring the family from commit trailers or the PR author (the old option b) is impossible: AGENTS.md forbids agent attribution trailers, and every PR author is joeharris76. Record the decision in docs/operations/oracle-review-v2.md. Decide this before the muse items (oracle-muse-invalid-verdict-output-20261009, oracle-self-attested-file-list-reviewers-20261008). Evidence: _project/scripts/oracle_reviewers/selection.py:60-64 (`excluded_families` falls back to `default_author_family`), .github/oracle-reviewers.yml:103-105 (tier orders).

The oracle skips reviewers of the same family as the PR's author (`selection.excluded_families`), reading `author-family:<family>` labels and falling back to `default_author_family: claude` (.github/oracle-reviewers.yml). On 2026-10-09 the repository had no `author-family:*` labels at all, and nothing in .github, scripts or _project/scripts applies one (`git grep author-family` finds only the policy key and the reviewer package). Every PR is therefore treated as claude-authored: claude reviewers are skipped everywhere, and a PR written by a codex or muse agent can be reviewed by codex or muse, which defeats the diversity rule. Found while running oracle canaries: the labels had to be created by hand to make muse the first eligible reviewer (canaries #2842 and #2845), and were deleted afterwards.

Guardrails. Never weaken the required oracle-review check. A label must not let an author choose a weaker reviewer: the tier order and allowed tiers still apply. Very-high tier for any change to the reviewer package or policy.
